name: Brigade Hotel Ventures Ltd
title: Brigade Hotel Ventures Ltd - 544457 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Brigade Hotel Ventures Q1 FY27 PAT rose 140% to INR17 crores on 9% RevPAR growth and lower finance cost, despite a ~INR14 crore West Asia-linked MICE cancellation hit.
summary.overview: Consolidated total income rose 5% YoY to INR131 crores and EBITDA rose 9% to INR46 crores at a 34.8% margin, with GST 2.0 weighing 1.6 points on margin. PAT more than doubled to INR17 crores from INR7 crores, mainly because finance cost fell over 50% to INR8.7 crores after post-IPO debt repayment. Operationally, ARR rose 7% to INR7,241 and occupancy rose 2% to 75.7%, with management calling the RevPAR growth rate-led. F&B was the weak spot as large MICE events were cancelled or postponed across the city, and management expects a stronger Q2 and H2.

financial_highlights.change: down from INR18.9 crores in Q1 FY26 (over 50%)
no institutional debt after INR468.1 crores repaid from IPO proceeds

segments.name: Bangalore hotels
segments.commentary: ARR grew about 3% and occupancy rose 8%, giving RevPAR growth of about 10%; management is holding occupancy and will push ADR over the next three quarters.

segments.name: Sheraton Grand (F&B-heavy)
segments.commentary: Roughly 50-50 room and F&B revenue mix; it took the largest F&B hit from MICE cancellations, and its ADR was about INR500 lower YoY.

segments.name: Courtyard by Marriott Kochi Infopark (ex Four Points)
segments.commentary: ARR rose to INR4,650 from INR4,200, but occupancy fell sharply (71% in Q1 FY26) due to lost crew business and GDS changes during rebranding; management sees occupancy in the high 60s in Q2 and expects at least 10% ADR growth this year.

segments.name: ibis Styles
segments.commentary: Occupancy was about 40% in its first half-year of operations and is now in the 70s in its second year.

guidance_outlook: Management is trying to hold mid-teens like-to-like revenue growth for FY27, with the Q1 shortfall (about INR14 crores, roughly 10% of top line) expected to be recouped in H2.
July performance described as better and September as very buoyant; management expects Q2 to be much stronger than Q1.
Q4 FY27 expected to be strong on large-scale MICE events, which recur every alternate year (Aero Show year).
ADR target of above INR7,500 for the portfolio and each hotel, to offset GST impact; Q1 FY26 ADR was INR6,761.
Management says the 1,700 upcoming keys take the portfolio from 1,600 to 3,300 keys by FY30/FY31; luxury and upper-upscale mix to reach 31% by FY29 and 38% by FY31.
Internal accruals expected to contribute over INR1,000 crores over the coming years, with the rest from borrowing (about 60:40 mix).
Hotel acquisition from IPO proceeds under discussion, with a transaction targeted in FY27 subject to due diligence.
capex_capacity: Total development capex of about INR3,600 crores; about INR400 crores spent in FY26 and INR500 crores planned for FY27. Q1 FY27 spend was about INR53 crores (INR45 crores CWIP, INR3.5 crores renovation, INR4 crores for the new restaurant Project Grain), with about INR350 crores to be spent over the remaining three quarters.
Courtyard by Marriott Chennai at World Trade Center, 45 keys, launch planned for October / Q3 FY27.

Two Fairfield hotels under construction; Ritz-Carlton Vaikom well underway with designs finalised; JW Marriott Chennai excavation to start soon; InterContinental at Brigade Gateway dependent on the mixed-use township.
Grand Hyatt slightly delayed from FY28 because of pending approvals; Tumkur Road (Bangalore) project waiting for approvals.
JW Marriott Chennai under approval and Thiruvananthapuram still in planning; management expects both to open by 2030.
Renewable energy at 61% of total energy needs; several hotels above 90%.
demand_pricing: Management attributes Q1 weakness to West Asia conflict, which cut foreign travellers (FTAs) from about 40% to about 30% of room arrivals and raised fares and fuel costs.
Cancellations and postponements of large MICE events hit the whole city; the INR14 crore impact was about 60% F&B and 40% rooms. MICE is about 15-18% of room bookings.
Domestic corporate business, locally negotiated rates, staycations, and social events were used to backfill room revenue.
Management says RevPAR growth was rate-led rather than occupancy-led, though occupancy rose in Bangalore and in most hotels.
F&B is about 32% of overall top line.
WTC Chennai expected to open at a minimum starting ADR of INR9,000 with stabilised occupancy of about 80%, backed by captive demand from tenants.

qa_highlights.question: How much capex was spent in Q1 and how will the INR500 crore FY27 plan be phased?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR53 crores was spent in Q1; about INR350 crores is expected in the remaining three quarters, mainly H2.

qa_highlights.question: Is the F&B and MICE trend improving for the rest of the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cites July pickup, very healthy September, and larger MICE inquiries, and expects the lost Q1 revenue to be partly recovered in H2.

qa_highlights.question: Will the mid-teens growth target for FY27 hold given the slow start and high base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management still aims for mid-teens like-to-like growth, citing the INR14 crore cancellation hit as the main gap; no revised number was given.

qa_highlights.question: Is Bangalore strength driven by domestic demand or business recovery?
qa_highlights.answer: Domestic accounts, locally negotiated rates, and staycations replaced lost foreign travellers; management says the portfolio occupancy is about 76% with five of nine hotels above 80%.

qa_highlights.question: Are there delays on live projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Mostly on track; the Grand Hyatt is slightly delayed pending approvals, and the Tumkur Road project awaits approvals.

qa_highlights.question: Should ADR be prioritised over occupancy in Bangalore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management wants to hold occupancy and grow ADR; it aims for the portfolio and each hotel to cross INR7,500 ADR.

risks_watch: Q2 and H2 recovery depends on MICE events being postponed rather than cancelled; management says July was better and September very buoyant, but no Q2 numbers were given.

Mid-teens like-to-like revenue growth for FY27 is still the target with no revised number, after an INR14 crore (about 10% of top line) Q1 shortfall; the high base in Q2 and Q3 is a risk to that target.
Courtyard by Marriott Kochi Infopark occupancy fell sharply on lost crew business and GDS changes during rebranding; recovery to the high 60s in Q2 and at least 10% ADR growth this year is unproven.

FTA share of room arrivals fell from about 40% to about 30% and West Asia fuel and fare pressure persists; ADR target of above INR7,500 for the portfolio and each hotel depends on this mix shift reversing.

Project timelines: Grand Hyatt slightly delayed from FY28 pending approvals, Tumkur Road awaiting approvals, InterContinental dependent on the Brigade Gateway township; JW Marriott Chennai and Thiruvananthapuram targeted by 2030.

Capex phasing: about INR350 crores of the INR500 crores FY27 plan is to be spent over the remaining three quarters after INR53 crores in Q1; acquisition from IPO proceeds targeted for FY27 subject to due diligence; leadership change with a new CEO (Vinay Gupta) joining after the COO's resignation.
key_quotes: Our RevPAR growth this quarter was rate-led rather than occupancy-led, which speaks to the quality and positioning of our assets rather than simply riding a favourable demand cycle.
What we are very hopeful of doing is making up the lost revenue in Q1 in the second half of the year.
We do expect a minimum of a INR9,000 as a starting ADR and then we expect that to grow in the coming months.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on the recovery outlook, repeatedly describing July as better and September as very buoyant and reiterating the mid-teens FY27 target. It was more cautious on Q1 specifics, attributing the F&B and MICE shortfall to the West Asia conflict and deferring figures for the new bar and restaurant and the Kochi occupancy recovery.
